title: Admin workflows and the first end-to-end test
author: pratos with Claude Code
summary: An admin can now see and steer the running product: a dashboard, every account, the event log with secrets masked, and the flags that switch behaviour on. Every page is an API call first, behind one admin check. The first Playwright test proves it in a real browser.
current: cp-03 ended with the engine (`packages/engine`), sign-up, sign-in and sign-out on it, and three seeded accounts: Admin, Sam and the agent. Accounts carry an `admin` bit, but nothing reads it yet, there are no flags, and no test drives a browser.
discoveries: `AccountOpened` records a `passwordHash` and `SignedIn` a `tokenHash`; the event log shows both unless the API masks every key matching hash, password or token.
A form submitted before React hydrates posts natively, so a test that types too early sees a reload. Tests wait for `<html data-hydrated>`.
`stream_events`, `accounts` and `sign_ins` are already in D1 from `0002_accounts.sql`, so the dashboard counts with plain SQL and needs no new projection.
`currentAccount` in `apps/api/src/auth.ts` already returns the `admin` bit, so `requireAdmin` is one more check on the same sign-in.
Under `just up` the API is reached only over the service binding, so pages and Playwright test it; nothing curls it yet.
endState: Signed in as Admin, `/admin` shows counts, accounts, the event log with `passwordHash="•••"`, and flags you can switch. Sam is refused with the reason. `just e2e admin` passes in Chromium against the migrated, seeded app.
notDoing: Writing accounts from the dashboard; `just user-add` opens them.
Reading flags in `decide()`; the first flagged command, `ResolveThread`, arrives at cp-05.
The screen asking which flags are on for someone; that waits for the release stage.
Recording flag changes as events; a change overwrites the D1 row.
approach: API first, because the page and any agent with an admin sign-in must do the same things. Then the pages over it, then the browser test that walks every refusal and the admin path.

spec.question: What happens when someone opens an admin page?
spec.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant W as Web Worker
  participant A as API
  participant D as D1
  B->>W: GET /admin, with the sign-in cookie
  W->>A: GET /admin/summary, cookie as bearer
  A->>D: who is this sign-in, are they admin?
  A-->>W: 401, 403 or the counts
  W-->>B: dashboard, or why it refused

steps.caption: The admin opens the dashboard, and the browser sends its sign-in cookie.
The web Worker asks the API, passing the cookie on as a bearer token.
requireAdmin looks up the sign-in and its admin bit in D1.
No sign-in gets 401, a participant 403, and an admin the counts.
The page shows the dashboard, or says why it refused and how to get in.

phases.name: API: flags and admin reads, admins only
phases.goal: `/flags`, `PUT /flags/:name` and `/admin/*` answer 401 without a sign-in, 403 for Sam, and data for Admin; secrets print as •••.

changes.intent: Create the flags table, default off; the file also holds the empty decisions projection.

contract.code:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS flags (
  name TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  allowlist TEXT,            -- participant ids, comma separated
  percent INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

changes.intent: Add Flags: on when enabled, allowlisted, or the participant's stable bucket is under percent.
Add `requireAdmin`: 401 without a sign-in, 403 naming the account that is not an admin.
FlagsAdmin over D1 or a Map; a bad name or percent is `FlagInvalid`, 400.
Summary counts, accounts with live sign-ins, newest events with hash, password and token masked.
Mount `/flags` and `/admin`; both sub-apps run `requireAdmin` on every route.
Set then list, an invalid percent, an empty name: all on the Map layer.
Seed `resolve-thread` off, allowlisted for admin and pratos, so the flags page has a row.
`just flag list | on | off | user | pct` against local D1, or remote with `GH_REMOTE=1`.

manual.text: `just flag pct demo 25`, then `just flag list` shows demo at 25%.

phases.notes: The justfile's `flag` recipe calls `scripts/flag.sh`; add it in the same change. The API has no port of its own under `just up` until cp-06 adds `/api`.

phases.name: Admin pages: four screens over the API
phases.goal: `/admin`, `/admin/accounts`, `/admin/events` and `/admin/flags` show API data to Admin and one sentence of refusal to everyone else.

One row per account with its role and live sign-ins; `data-account` holds the participant id.
